claims.quote: A postal packet's dip-dial records every yard of every run.
claims.description: Every vehicle automatically records a continuous trace of its flight path for later analysis by a central authority.

claims.quote: And minute by minute our silent clock gives us a sixteen-second mile.
claims.description: Aircraft will routinely cruise at about 225 miles per hour.

claims.quote: But some day—even on the Equator—we shall hold the Sun level in his full stride.
claims.description: Humans will be able to lengthen the dawn or hold the Sun in place in the sky over any latitude.

claims.quote: The deep-sea freighters are rising to lung up after the long night, and the leisurely ocean is all patterned with peacock's eyes of foam.
claims.description: Freight ships will routinely submerge and resurface, carrying cargo beneath the ocean as well as on it.

claims.quote: We hoist 'em in sterilized air for a while.
claims.description: Tuberculosis patients will be treated by living for a time in high-altitude air kept sterile, lifted above the microbes of low ground.

claims.quote: Practically, the A. B. C. confirms or annuls all international arrangements and, to judge from its last report, finds our tolerant, humorous, lazy little planet only too ready to shift the whole burden of public administration on its shoulders.
claims.description: A single world body of aerial traffic control will confirm or annul all international arrangements and run public administration for the whole planet.

claims.quote: We have been treated to the spectacle of what are practically keeled racing-planes driven a clear five foot or more above the water
claims.description: Racing boats will be lifted clear of the water on keeled planes, a hydrofoil-like design.

claims.quote: Trans-Asiatic Directs we met, soberly ringing the world round the Fiftieth Meridian at an honest seventy knots
claims.description: Long-haul aerial freight will circle the globe at about seventy knots.
